name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,378

clue.text: Vehicle days on station? This may be sent home

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another comes after it in the row

blocks.note: a post is a station, as a sentry's post
a car is the everyday vehicle
d is the standard abbreviation for day or days

explanation.surface: A traveller spends days waiting at a railway station and wonders what to send home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' reads as a railway stop, but here it is a post, as in a soldier's post; CAR and D then sit on it to give POSTCARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Holidaymakers traditionally mail a picture card back to family, so it is something typically dispatched homeward.

clue.text: Father’s green-coloured in sea voyage

blocks.note: pa is father, with the possessive s kept
sage is a grey-green colour, like the herb's leaves

explanation.surface: Dad turns green with seasickness on a boat trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests seasickness, but 'green-coloured' is simply SAGE, joined to PA'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a journey by ship, as in booking a passage across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Drop off some letter entailing extra postage initially

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so keep the opening of each word

blocks.note: the first letters of five consecutive words

explanation.surface: A post office clerk warns that a heavy letter will need extra stamps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop off' looks like posting a letter, but it is the definition: to fall asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is an idiom for falling asleep, so it matches the verb meaning to rest unconscious.

clue.text: Device, something to stop pregnancy shunned by church

indicators.note: to be shunned is to be kept away, so those letters are left out

blocks.note: birth control in one word
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A comment on the church's disapproval of birth control devices.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a real piece of church teaching; in the wordplay the church is merely CE, removed from CONTRACEPTION to leave CONTRAPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraption is a machine or gadget, often a strange or improvised one.

clue.text: Restore theatre song

blocks.note: rep is repertory theatre
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Someone wants to revive an old stage song.
explanation.walkthrough: Repertory theatre, a company staging a rotating set of plays, is shortened to REP.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something broken is to fix or mend it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Massage following last of fattening food

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so keep only that
something following comes after, so it is placed later in the answer

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
a rub is a massage

explanation.surface: A spa treatment after a rich meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fattening food' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits it: 'last of fattening' gives G, and 'food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal slang for things to eat, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Book place to watch game

blocks.note: to book a seat or table is to secure it in advance
a protected park where wild animals can be viewed on safari

explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests a sports match and 'place to watch' a stadium, but game here is wild animals, as in a game reserve on safari.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table is to secure it ahead; a nature park where animals are protected and viewed has the same name.

clue.text: Rubbish for instance library turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: e.g. means for instance
lib. is a standard abbreviation for library

explanation.surface: Someone discovers junk in a library, perhaps the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as 'appeared', but in a down clue it means written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is nonsense or worthless talk, named for the dirty water in a ship's hull.

clue.text: Ship’s back badly set by Royal Navy

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out jumbled
one thing placed beside another follows it, so the pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: anagram fodder, three letters
RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval vessel's hull has been poorly built by the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface stays at sea, which hides that 'set' is just three letters to rearrange before adding RN.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a boat, the opposite end from the bow.

clue.text: Standard form of Laos sunshade

indicators.note: a new form of letters is a reshaping, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in golf
anagram fodder, four letters

explanation.surface: The usual way to keep off the sun in Laos.
explanation.walkthrough: Laos is a country in Southeast Asia, but its name here is just four letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella carried to give shade from strong sunlight.

clue.text: Seek to preserve rare fig tree that’s damaged

indicators.note: damaged goods are broken up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eleven letters

explanation.surface: A conservationist tries to save an uncommon, ailing fig tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about protecting a plant; the definition is about keeping food cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilling food in a fridge is done to stop it spoiling, so it is an attempt to keep it fresh.

clue.text: A representative unit used in grids

blocks.note: the article kept as it is
an MP, a Member of Parliament, represents a constituency

explanation.surface: A delegate is a member of some network of grids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grids' suggests crossword grids, but these are electrical grids, which carry current measured in amps.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere measures electric current, which power networks carry across the country.

clue.text: Control police stress

blocks.note: to rein in is to control, as with a horse
a police force

explanation.surface: A complaint about the pressure of keeping police in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' reads as a noun about pressure, but it is a verb: to emphasise a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline or emphasise an argument is to strengthen it, the verb sense of both words.

clue.text: Versace regularly copy — avoid

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: Advice to shun fashion knock-offs of the Italian designer label.
explanation.walkthrough: Versace is an Italian fashion house, and designer copies are fakes; here its even letters give ESC.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape a fate or duty is to dodge or evade it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Depressed on being in cold underground chamber

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: C for cold, as on a tap
kept as it is
a cave is a natural chamber below ground

explanation.surface: Someone feels low while trapped in a chilly cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' reads as gloomy, but it is the physical sense: sunken or pressed inwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A concave surface curves inward like the inside of a bowl, so it is sunken or dented.

clue.text: One good in open flying?

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another
letters sent flying are scattered, so they land in a new order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
g is a standard abbreviation for good
anagram fodder, four letters

explanation.surface: Someone who is good at flying in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: I and G go inside a rearranged OPEN, and a pigeon is indeed good at flying in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue describes a bird skilled on the wing out of doors, which suits the common town bird.

clue.text: Garment close to neckwear

blocks.note: nigh is an old word for near
a tie is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing that sits near a tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like a positional link, but it supplies NIGH, meaning near.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, an item of clothing worn to bed.

clue.text: Excellent first two-thirds of US football championship match

indicators.note: keeping only the first two-thirds drops the final third of the letters

blocks.note: the Super Bowl, the annual final of American football

explanation.surface: A fan praises the first two periods of the big championship game.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPERBOWL has nine letters, so two-thirds is six; the last three, OWL, go.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means outstanding or first-rate, a straight adjective synonym for top quality.

clue.text: What’s glued into altered map can show this

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: Someone has pasted something into a doctored map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered map' looks like one phrase, but 'altered' works backwards on 'glued into', and 'map' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maps carry meridian lines giving east-west position, measured in degrees from Greenwich.

clue.text: See about excessive style of bingo

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look or see
OTT, over the top, is British slang for excessive

explanation.surface: A complaint about an overdone bingo night.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT stands for over the top, a common British way of saying excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance where numbered cards are marked as numbers are drawn, much like bingo.

clue.text: Catch burbot and gurnard to begin with

indicators.note: what comes to begin with is at the start, so take opening letters

blocks.note: the first letters of three words

explanation.surface: An angler hopes to land a couple of fish species to start the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Burbot and gurnard are real fish, which makes 'Catch' look like fishing; the definition is catch as a verb, to bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunters speak of bagging game, meaning capturing or securing it.

clue.text: Inflate vessel outside loch

indicators.note: one thing outside another surrounds it, so it wraps round

blocks.note: a boat is a vessel
L is an abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: Pumping up an inflatable boat beside a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A loch is a Scottish lake; like lake, it abbreviates to L.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell or puff something up with air or gas is to make it bigger.

clue.text: Fall in support for person learning on the job

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball
rain is a fall, as in a rainfall

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tumble and needs a helping hand at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' reads as a tumble, but it is rain; 'support' is the golf tee a ball rests on.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice or beginner being taught skills while employed is exactly who this describes.

clue.text: Concerning blood type forbidden

blocks.note: AB is one of the blood groups
out means not allowed, as in 'that's out'

explanation.surface: Worry over a banned blood group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concerning' reads as worrying, but it is the preposition meaning on the subject of.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are prepositions meaning regarding or on the topic of something.

clue.text: Sign me on working

indicators.note: letters being worked are handled and moved about, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, four letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be signed up for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign me on' reads as enlisting, but 'Sign' is the definition and 'working' stirs the letters of ME ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent or indication of what is to come.

clue.text: An insect protecting unusual nest — one not here

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged
to protect is to shield all round, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: the article as a single letter
a bee is an insect
anagram fodder, four letters

explanation.surface: A bee guards its odd nest, but one member of the colony is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect surface flows into the definition, making 'one not here' seem like a missing bee.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is away or missing from where they should be.
